features.description: A finite content clause introduced by invariant ðæt fills the content complement of the selected knowing/saying verb.
features.scope_note: Keep distinct from determiner/relative ðæt; clause has its own subject and finite verb.

features.description: Reported content commonly uses subjunctive; a proposition asserted as fact may use indicative.
features.scope_note: Exercises must name the communicative stance when a specific mood is required; subjunctive does not mean the report is false.

features.description: In a report, recover referents and the time of the reported situation from the stated context; adjust person accordingly.
features.scope_note: Limited simultaneous present/past reports only. No universal English-style backshift, automatic pronoun replacement, or systematic tense-sequence doctrine; advanced Unit12 scope remains deferred.

features.description: Wh question clauses can be complements of witan or sęcgan, including Saga mē + wh clause. The wh form takes its internal case.
features.scope_note: This is an embedded question, not an ordinary relative antecedent construction. Subjunctive is a normal selected reporting/question pattern; factual indicative is defensible in suitable context.

features.description: Invariant hwæðer introduces a dependent yes/no question after witan/sęcgan.
features.scope_note: Distinct lemma/sense from inflected hwæðer which of two. No direct-question use of the new conjunction is inferred.

features.description: Hātan command takes accusative actor + plain infinitive. The infinitive may retain its own accusative object.
features.scope_note: Select hātan for II.12.5; no unnecessary gebēodan system. Dative reporting addressee is a different function.

features.description: Gesēon can take an accusative actor and a plain infinitive describing the perceived action.
features.scope_note: The actor belongs to the infinitival event; no claim that every verb takes this construction.

features.description: Gewyrcean may take an accusative object and an agreeing accusative predicate adjective.
features.scope_note: Contrast prior hātan naming two-accusative construction; morphology must agree with the object, not the main subject.

features.description: Preterite subjunctive can express a wish contrary to the present situation, including Wǣre ic ...!
features.scope_note: Promotes bounded previously recognition-only nonpast unreal use. No general counterfactual conditional or pluperfect system.

features.description: Dative experiencer + lēofre is + plain infinitive expresses a preference; the comparison may contain parallel mid+dative phrases.
features.scope_note: Only this attested preference frame is productive; broad impersonal constructions are not inferred.

features.description: Sęcgan can name its recipient in the dative with direct speech or a dependent content/question complement.
Predicative headless ðæt means what/that which in be what one is/ought to be, without a separate expressed antecedent.
features.scope_note: Bounded identity/role pattern for II.11.5–6; not a general free-choice system or the statement conjunction.

features.description: A group may be named by personal genitive after substantival hwilc or sume; hīe sume is also Cook’s appositional some-of-them expression.
features.scope_note: Promote personal ēower only in this frame; prior hiera morphology is reused. No blanket personal-genitive syntax promotion.

features.description: Use on + accusative to locate an event on a numbered day.
features.scope_note: Prior supplied temporal sense promoted; this does not replace ordinary location on+dative.

features.description: Mid + dative names an accompanying person or cargo.
features.scope_note: Means/manner/abstract circumstance require their own prior or supplied records.

features.description: For-ðām introduces an indicative factual reason clause.
features.scope_note: Source spelling retained; no new consequence-purpose equivalence.

features.description: A predicate adjective referring jointly to subjects of different grammatical genders is normally neuterplural.
features.scope_note: II.9.6 has masculine ęle and neuter wīn; selected predicate is neuterplural gōd. Explain normal pattern without claiming exceptionless agreement.

features.description: Ne + willan expresses unwillingness/refusal; translate the sense from context.
features.scope_note: Use prior positive forms with ne; no additional negative contraction paradigm or future auxiliary system assigned.

features.description: Use prior tēon with accusative object plus forð to express produce/bring forth.
features.scope_note: Plain infinitive after hātan and hortative subjunctive use prior tēon forms; no new separable-prefix system taught.

features.description: Fręmman in the benefit sense governs the beneficiary in the dative.
Slēan may express making a stroke without naming an object.
features.scope_note: Bounded ordinary striking use for the hammer; prior accusative-object construction is not erased.

features.description: Complete present/preterite indicative systems of the seventeen explicitly selected new trade/narrative verbs.
features.scope_note: 204 cells. Citation infinitives do not license unassigned nonfinite production; wician plain infinitive is separately productive.

features.description: Complete singular/plural commands of rōwan, bycgan, sēcan, begān, gestillan and rǣdan.
features.scope_note: 12 cells; sēceað is a separately declared source recognition variant.

features.description: Complete present/preterite subjunctive of sēcan.
features.scope_note: 12 cells; present firstplural hortative required by II.9.12; no automatic teaching of every subordinate-clause use.

features.description: Recognize exact sēceað as the plural command variant of selected sēcað.
